chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Improvising as self-expression; never missing a night
summary: Dance calls it self-expression; Norvo says musicians never miss work for illness and improvising kept every job fresh.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well, really Red. I think actually what it is in a way, it's self-expression.
It's self-expression, that's why it's so -- you know what I mean, it's just you -- you just open up and out it comes. It's Not work. It's --
You have no control over it, you really have no --
Yeah, that's right, you have no control.

Course I think sometimes you're better than others. And yet, musicians never have excuses for being sick. I never missed a day in my life of being sick. I could have a temperature and the flu and everything, but I went to work.
It was hard to get dressed --
There's something happens and I don't --
-- and yet sometimes I think I do. I don't know if I don't -- if I do. I know I'm not really sure about that, but I know that -- that has been the delightful part all these years.
-- and playing with different things and ah -- ah, the improvising has been the thing.

Yeah, I think it is, too. But -- because this is a very important thing, what we're talking about right now and it would be nice if we had a -- had a little more on the tape, but I think I'll let it run maybe, because we're going to let -- going to turn it over, so I'll let it go through.
